passages.title: Base N Break (Oliver Kell) — Consolidation at EMA Before Continuation
passages.text:
The Base N' Break is Oliver Kell's continuation entry in the Cycle of Price Action. After the initial Wedge Pop and EMA Crossback, the stock finds support at the moving averages and consolidates (bases) before the next leg up.

CRITERIA:
- Stock in established uptrend (already had Wedge Pop and EMA Crossback)
- Consolidation of 1-4+ weeks at or above the 10/20 EMA
- Price contraction (tightening range) during the base
- Volume dries up during the base (accumulation without distribution)
- Break

passages.title: Gil Morales Pocket Pivot Exact Criteria
passages.text: Pocket Pivot Definition: Volume on the up day must exceed the highest volume of ANY DOWN DAY in the prior 10 trading sessions. Entry: At or near the 10-DMA (within 1-2% of 10-DMA). Best combo: Volume Dry-Up (VDU) followed immediately by Pocket Pivot = highest probability signal (supply exhausted, then institutional demand arrives).

passages.title: Gil Morales Pocket Pivot — Exact Criteria and Definition
passages.text: Definition: an up-day in price where the volume exceeds the highest single down-day volume of the prior 10 trading days. Purpose: identifies stealth institutional accumulation that is not visible as a classical breakout.

passages.title: Gil Morales Pocket Pivot — Entry and Requirements
passages.text: Entry: buy on the day of the pocket pivot signal or the next day if confirming price action. Requirements: stock must be in a base or just coming out of one. Price should be above the 10-day and 50-day moving averages.

passages.title: Gil Morales Pocket Pivot — Stop and Key Nuance
passages.text: Stop: below the 10-day moving average (close below the 10 DMA = exit). Key nuance: pocket pivots that occur near the low of a base are MORE significant than those at the top — institutions are building early.

passages.title: Cross-Reference: Qullamaggie EP vs Morales Pocket Pivot
passages.text: Both identify unusual institutional volume. The EP is a gap-up event; the Pocket Pivot is a subtle accumulation signal within a base. Pocket Pivots often PRECEDE an EP — if you see multiple pocket pivots in a base, watch for the eventual EP catalyst.

passages.title: Gil Morales Pocket Pivot (Setup 11)
passages.text: ...er the prior 10 trading sessions. This signals institutional buying is stepping in during a pullback. Entry: Buy on the pocket pivot day itself or on a pullback to the pocket pivot price level. Stop: Below the 50-day MA or below the most recent swing low. Key: This is an EARLY entry signal — before the traditional breakout. Gives better risk/reward but requires more conviction.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot as Early Entry Signal
passages.text: The pocket pivot is an EARLY entry signal — before the traditional breakout. It gives better risk/reward but requires more conviction. Up-volume on the pocket pivot day must exceed the largest down-volume day over the prior 10 trading sessions.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot Critical Differentiator
passages.text: Pocket Pivot critical differentiator: Volume exceeds any down-day volume in prior 10 sessions while within the base. This volume signature signals institutional buying within the base before the traditional breakout.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot Failure Mode 1: Average Volume Confusion
passages.text: Volume exceeds prior down-day volume but is AVERAGE for recent up-days — not a true Pocket Pivot, just a normal up day. The PP requires the volume to exceed ALL down-day volume in the prior 10 sessions, not just be above average. This is a strict test; average up-day volume that happens to exceed down-day volume is noise.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot Failure Mode 2: Distribution Masquerade
passages.text: Price action on the PP day closes in the lower half of the day's range. Absorption was for distribution, not accumulation. A genuine PP must close in the upper half of the range — it shows that buying interest is strong enough to maintain price through the day.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot Failure Mode 3: Extended Base Entry
passages.text: Taking the PP in a leading stock that is already extended from its base. Pocket Pivots work best WITHIN the base or on the first pullback after a breakout — not after a 30%+ run. An extended stock using a PP as a re-entry is operating on reduced R:R and reduced institutional support.

passages.title: Pocket Pivot Volume Quality: Distribution Across Session Matters
passages.text: Pocket Pivot volume quality confirmation now matters as much as quantity. Volume should be distributed across the session, not entirely front-loaded. A PP with 80% of volume in the first 30 minutes and fading action is lower quality than a PP with consistent volume across the full day. Classic teaching required volume above all down-day volume in the prior 10 sessions — this remains necessary but insufficient without session distribution check.
